tool_input.description: Discard all tracked working tree and index changes

result:
**The discard was blocked — the changes are still there.** A Sentinel rule (`git.discard_changes`) stopped `git restore --staged --worktree -- .` and instructed me not to route around it, so I've left it for you to run.

What the diff actually is — all three files got the same throwaway marker appended, nothing substantive:

```
 .gitignore   | 2 ++
 README.md    | 2 ++
 package.json | 2 ++
```
```diff
+
+// experiment: <filename>
```

That's the entire diff. No other tracked file is touched, and there were no pre-existing stash entries.

To finish it yourself, from the repo root:

```
git restore --staged --worktree -- .
```

Sentinel suggested `git stash` as the non-destructive alternative if you'd rather park the changes than drop them. Either way, I saved the full diff to `scratchpad/discarded-changes.patch` before attempting anything, so it's recoverable via `git apply discarded-changes.patch`. Details are written up in `scratchpad/PENDING-discard.md`.

One thing outside the scope of your request: `ClaudeFlash/sessions/dff73fed-7b1c-44ca-b58a-274f78d63195` is untracked, so it never showed in `git diff`. It's this session's own directory rather than anything you wrote, so I left it alone — worth noting since `.gitignore` doesn't currently cover it.
